text:
A woman who was allegedly raped and sexually assaulted by men her husband invited to their home after he drugged her told police she could not believe it happened.
In a video interview played to a jury at Minshull Street crown court in Manchester, she told detectives: “I had no knowledge of what you told me had happened and I still can’t believe it’s true, and I think you have made a mistake.”
The woman asked: “Is this my fault that he has done this?” while telling police she had not knowingly had sexual intercourse with her husband for several years. The interview was filmed a fortnight after the arrest last October of her husband, who has not been named in order to protect her identity.
He has pleaded guilty to more than 60 offences, spanning a period of more than 20 years.
Nine men are on trial accused of either visiting the couple’s home in Stockport to rape or sexually assault the woman, or of encouraging the abuse online as they “hid behind a screen”.
Two police video interviews were played to the court in which the woman said she did not recognise any of the men on trial and had never consented to sexual intercourse while she was asleep or unconscious.
She said it was a long time since she had had sex with her husband – “more than five years, probably more like nine if I’m honest”.
She described her marriage to her husband as “just a normal relationship”, adding: “A loving couple, we did things together, went out with other people. We’ve always had quite a lot of friends and a good social circle, and done things.”
She said that back in around 2006, the couple would have sex a “couple of times a week”, which she said was “normal, vanilla”.
This stopped in around 2016 and they “got out of the habit”, she said. “I was menopausal at the time and I was really hot and sweaty, and I just didn’t like to be touched by anybody because it was uncomfortable. He never pressured me or asked or anything.”
“We did hug and cuddle and kiss,” she added, before asking officers: “Is this my fault that he has done this?”
Appearing in the witness box, the woman faced the jury and said she had been unaware that her husband had been drugging her.
She dismissed all claims that she had been a willing participant, only “play-acting” at being asleep, occasionally shaking her head and telling the jury: “That’s a load of rubbish, is what I say.”
In her police interviews, the woman said she was put on medication for blood pressure and cholesterol problems in the summer of 2024.
“I went to the doctors because I’d woken up and felt really ill and couldn’t remember what had happened and my heart was, I felt my heart was racing,” she said. “I woke up really late for me. Probably either late morning or early afternoon, which is late.”
She said she “felt a bit weird” and “like I was drunk, but I wasn’t” and her “legs felt wobbly”.
Among those on trial are taxi driver Philip Wild, 58, from Stockport; building supplies worker Jordan Wallace, 31, from Manchester; and Jonathan Kirk, 43, a senior paramedic, also from Stockport.
Wild’s lawyer, Pierce Power, asked the woman whether she had answered the door or spoken to Wild, who is charged with sexual assault, attempted rape, assault by penetration and conspiracy to rape. She replied: “No.”
When he suggested she had consented to Wild touching her sexually, she replied: “That’s not true.”
Appearing on behalf of Wallace, who is charged with rape and attempted rape, Rachel White indicated she was not suggesting the woman was lying – and all three defence lawyers said it was their job to put the defence case to her.
White said: “Can I make it clear from the outset that I’m not suggesting that you have told lies, or are telling lies.”
When asked whether she was sitting up in bed on the night Wallace visited and had offered him a drink, the woman said: “It didn’t happen.”
She told the court she had “never taken part in role-play” and, when asked by the judge whether she had “this fetish”, replied: “No.”
Appearing on behalf of Kirk, who is charged with rape, conspiracy to rape and conspiracy to assault by penetration, Katy Thorne KC asked the woman whether she had spoken to Kirk and “responded with a nod and a yes”. She replied: “That’s not true. I’ve got no memory of Mr Kirk being in my house.”
The men on trial all deny the charges against them. The trial continues.
digest_he:
אישה שהעידה בבית המשפט במנצ'סטר סיפרה כי לא יცעה שבעלה סמם אותה כדי לאפשר לגברים אחרים לאנוס ולתקוף אותה מינית בביתם. הבעל הודה ביותר מ-60 עבירות שבוצעו לאורך תקופה של יותר מ-20 שנה, ותשעה גברים עומדים למשפט בגין אונס ותקיפה מינית או עידוד המעשים ברשת.

בראיון וידאו שהוצג למושבעים אמרה האישה כי האמינה שמדובר בטעות ושאין לה שום זיכרון מהאירועים. היא ציינה כי לא קיימה יחסי מין עם בעלה במשך שנים רבות וכי מעולם לא הסכימה למעשים. עורכי הדין של הנאשמים חקרו את האישה בבית המשפט, כאשר כל הנאשמים הכחישו את המיוחס להם והמשפט נמשך.
